title: Simple and Compound Interest, Net Worth and Incentives
seo_title: Grade 7 Simple and Compound Interest, Net Worth and Incentives Worksheets (TEKS 7.13, STAAR)
standard_text: 7.13C create and organize a financial assets and liabilities record and construct a net worth statement; 7.13E calculate and compare simple interest and compound interest earnings; 7.13F analyze and compare monetary incentives, including sales, rebates, and coupons
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 personal financial literacy worksheets for Texas TEKS 7.13C, 7.13E and 7.13F: assets, liabilities and net worth, simple and compound interest, sales, rebates and coupons. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Net worth = assets − liabilities. Simple interest I = Prt.
key_sub: Compound interest earns interest on interest: $1,000 at 10% for 2 years = $1,210.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Assets are things of value you own; liabilities are debts you owe. Net worth = assets − liabilities.
  • Simple interest: I = Prt (principal × rate × time in years).
  • Compound interest earns interest on the interest too: multiply by (1 + rate) each year.
  • Compare deals by finding the final price: sales and coupons lower the price now; rebates give money back later.

Examples

Example

$1,000 at 5% simple interest for 3 years

1,000 × 0.05 × 3

Answer: $150

Example

$1,000 at 10% compounded yearly for 2 years

1,000 × 1.1 × 1.1

Answer: $1,210

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding liabilities to net worthSubtract what you owe from what you own.
Forgetting to multiply by the yearsI = Prt: use the number of years.
Treating compound interest like simple interestEach year's interest is added before the next year.

faq.q: Why does compound interest earn more?
faq.a: Interest is added to the balance, so next year's interest is on a bigger amount.

items.q: What is net worth?
c: The value of assets minus liabilities
Income minus expenses for one month

items.q: Which is an asset?
items.e: The house is an asset; the mortgage is a liability.

items.q: Which is an asset?
items.e: An asset is something of value that you own.

items.q: Which is a liability?
c: A balance owed on a credit card

items.q: Which is a liability?
items.e: Money still owed on a loan is a liability.

items.q: What does a negative net worth mean?
c: The person owns more than they owe
The person owes more than they own
